MNEM.coronary-a: Right coronary → SA node in ~60%. LAD = "widow-maker" (anterior wall of the left ventricle).
MNEM.vertebral-a: Ascends through the transverse foramina of C6–C1; joins its partner to form the basilar artery.

lig-acetabular-labrum: Fibrocartilage ring on the acetabular rim
Deepens the socket and seals the joint
Labral tears cause catching groin pain (FAI).
lig-acromioclavicular-ligament: AC separation ("separated shoulder") grades depend on AC ± coracoclavicular tears.
lig-annular-ligament-of-radius: Ring around the radial head, attached to the ulna
Holds the radial head while it spins in pronation/supination
"Nursemaid's elbow": radial head slips out of it when a toddler is pulled by the hand.
lig-anterior-cruciate-ligament: Anterior intercondylar area of tibia → medial side of the lateral femoral condyle
Stops the tibia sliding forward on the femur; resists hyperextension and rotation
Anterior drawer / Lachman test. Torn in pivoting non-contact injuries — "pop" and rapid swelling. "LAMP": Lateral (femur) Anterior, Medial Posterior for ACL/PCL femoral attachments.
lig-anterior-longitudinal-ligament: Fronts of vertebral bodies and discs, skull base → sacrum
Broad and strong — whiplash hyperextension can tear it.
lig-anterior-sacro-iliac-ligament: Pelvic (anterior) surface of the sacrum → ilium, just in front of the auricular surface
Thin thickening of the front of the SI joint capsule; resists the sacral base tipping forward (nutation) and the front of the joint gapping
Weakest of the three SI ligaments — strength order: interosseous > posterior > anterior. Stretches in pregnancy (relaxin) and is a common source of SI joint pain.
lig-anterior-talofibular-ligament: Lateral malleolus → neck of the talus
Resists inversion with the foot plantarflexed
The MOST commonly sprained ligament in the body (inversion sprain). Lateral ankle ligaments "ATFL, CFL, PTFL" tear in that order.
lig-anterior-tibiofibular-ligament: Front of the distal tibia → lateral malleolus
lig-arcuate-popliteal-ligament: Fibular head → arches over the popliteus tendon
lig-articular-capsule-of-elbow-joint: Encloses humero-ulnar, humeroradial and proximal radio-ulnar joints
lig-articular-capsule-of-glenohumeral-jo: Glenoid rim → anatomical neck of the humerus
Loose capsule allows huge range of motion (least stable joint)
Weakest inferiorly — most dislocations are anterior-inferior.
lig-articular-capsule-of-hip-joint: Acetabular rim → intertrochanteric line (front) and femoral neck (back)
lig-articular-capsule-of-interphalangeal: Stabilises the interphalangeal joints of foot
lig-articular-capsule-of-knee-joint: Femur → tibia, enclosing the condyles; patella sits in its front wall
Encloses the largest synovial joint (hinge with some rotation)
lig-articular-capsules-of-distal-interph: Stabilises the interphalangeal joints of foot
Stabilises the interphalangeal joints of hand
lig-articular-capsules-of-proximal-inter: Stabilises the interphalangeal joints of foot
Stabilises the interphalangeal joints of hand
lig-articular-disc-of-distal-radio-ulnar: Ulnar notch of radius → ulnar styloid (TFCC)
Triangular fibrocartilage: cushions the ulnar side of the wrist
TFCC tears cause ulnar-sided wrist pain.
lig-articular-disc-of-temporomandibular-: Between mandibular condyle and articular eminence
Divides the TMJ into two cavities; allows gliding + hinging
lig-calcaneofibular-ligament: Tip of the lateral malleolus → lateral calcaneus
Resists inversion; crosses both ankle and subtalar joints
Second to tear in an inversion sprain (after the ATFL).
lig-collateral-interphalangeal-ligaments: Stabilises the interphalangeal joints of foot
Stabilises the interphalangeal joints of hand
lig-conoid-ligament: Coracoid process → conoid tubercle of the clavicle
Suspends the scapula from the clavicle
Coracoclavicular = conoid (medial, cone-shaped) + trapezoid (lateral). Torn in a high-grade "separated shoulder".
lig-coraco-acromial-ligament: Forms the coraco-acromial arch over the humeral head
Supraspinatus tendon impinges under this arch.
lig-coracohumeral-ligament: Coracoid process → greater and lesser tubercles
Supports the top of the joint; limits lateral rotation
lig-costoclavicular-ligament: Main stabiliser of the SC joint; fulcrum for clavicle movement
lig-deep-part-of-tibial-collateral-ligam: Femur and tibia via the medial meniscus (meniscofemoral/meniscotibial fibres)
Anchors the medial meniscus; resists valgus stress
Deep MCL attaches to the medial meniscus — why MCL and medial meniscus tears go together.
lig-deep-transverse-metacarpal-ligament: Joins the palmar plates of MCP joints 2–5
lig-descending-part-of-iliofemoral-ligam: AIIS → lower intertrochanteric line (stem of the "Y")
lig-extensor-retinaculum-of-wrist: Holds the extensor tendons in six compartments
lig-external-intercostal-membrane: Continues the external intercostal muscles anteriorly to the sternum
lig-fibular-collateral-ligament: Lateral femoral epicondyle → head of the fibula
The LCL is a free round cord — NOT attached to the lateral meniscus, so the lateral meniscus is more mobile and less often torn.
lig-flexor-retinaculum-of-ankle: Roofs the tarsal tunnel ("Tom, Dick And Very Nervous Harry")
Tarsal tunnel syndrome = tibial nerve compression here.
lig-glenoid-labrum: SLAP tear (superior labrum) / Bankart lesion after dislocation.
lig-iliolumbar-ligament: Transverse process of L5 → iliac crest
lig-inferior-extensor-retinaculum-of-ank: Y-shaped band from the calcaneus over the dorsum of the foot
Prevents bowstringing of the extensor tendons
lig-inferior-fibular-retinaculum: Holds the fibular tendons on the calcaneus
lig-inferior-transverse-scapular-ligamen: Stabilises the fibrous joints of pectoral girdle
lig-interclavicular-ligament: Joins both clavicles across the jugular notch
lig-intercornual-ligament: Stabilises the fibrous joints of vertebral column
lig-internal-intercostal-membrane: Continues the internal intercostal muscles posteriorly to the vertebrae
lig-interosseous-sacro-iliac-ligament: Sacral tuberosity ↔ iliac tuberosity, deep to the posterior SI ligament
Strongest SI ligament; suspends the sacrum between the ilia and carries body weight to the pelvis
Order of strength: interosseous > posterior > anterior.
lig-intra-articular-ligament-of-head-of-: Stabilises the joint of head of rib
lig-ischiofemoral-ligament: The hip ligaments spiral and tighten in extension — the stable "screw-home" standing position.
lig-lateral-meniscus: Nearly circular ("O") fibrocartilage on the lateral tibial plateau
Deepens the tibial surface, absorbs shock
More mobile than the medial meniscus (popliteus pulls it back) so less often torn.
lig-lateral-temporomandibular-ligament: Prevents posterior displacement of the condyle
lig-ligament-of-head-of-femur: Acetabular notch → fovea of the femoral head
Carries a small artery to the femoral head (important in children)
lig-ligamenta-flava: Yellow elastic ligaments that help straighten the spine from flexion
Pierced in a lumbar puncture ("loss of resistance" for epidurals). Order: skin → supraspinous → interspinous → ligamentum flavum → epidural space.
lig-medial-meniscus: C-shaped fibrocartilage on the medial tibial plateau
Deepens the tibial surface, absorbs shock
"C" shaped and fixed to the MCL — torn more often than the lateral meniscus ("O"-shaped, mobile).
lig-median-cricothyroid-ligament: Stabilises the fibrous joints of larynx
lig-nuchal-ligament: External occipital protuberance → spinous processes of C1–C7
Midline attachment for trapezius and splenius; holds the head up
lig-oblique-cord: Ulnar tuberosity → radius below the radial tuberosity
Small band above the interosseous membrane
lig-oblique-popliteal-ligament: Expansion of the semimembranosus tendon → lateral femoral condyle
Strengthens the back of the capsule; resists hyperextension
lig-obturator-membrane: The obturator canal at its top transmits the obturator nerve and vessels.
lig-palmar-aponeurosis: Palmaris longus tendon → slips to the fingers
Dupuytren contracture = thickening that pulls the ring/little fingers into flexion.
lig-palmar-interphalangeal-ligaments: Stabilises the interphalangeal joints of hand
lig-plantar-aponeurosis: Medial calcaneal tubercle → fibrous slips to the toes
Ties the ends of the longitudinal arch together (windlass mechanism)
Plantar fasciitis: heel pain on the first steps in the morning.
lig-plantar-calcaneocuboid-ligament: "Short plantar ligament": supports the lateral arch
lig-plantar-interphalangeal-ligaments: Stabilises the interphalangeal joints of foot
lig-posterior-cruciate-ligament: Posterior intercondylar area of tibia → lateral side of the medial femoral condyle
Stops the tibia sliding backward; the knee's main stabiliser when flexed
Posterior drawer test. "Dashboard injury" — the tibia is driven back with the knee bent.
lig-posterior-layer-of-thoracolumbar-fas: Spinous processes → lateral raphe; origin of latissimus dorsi
Wraps the erector spinae; transmits force between latissimus dorsi and gluteus maximus
The thoracolumbar fascia ties the upper and lower limbs together across the back.
lig-posterior-longitudinal-ligament: Backs of vertebral bodies, axis → sacrum
Limits flexion; narrower in the lumbar region
Narrow lumbar PLL is why discs herniate posterolaterally (pressing on the nerve root).
lig-posterior-sacro-iliac-ligament: Posterior superior iliac spine → lateral sacral crest (short and long parts)
The long posterior SI ligament can be felt just below the PSIS — a classic SI pain point.
lig-posterior-talofibular-ligament: Malleolar fossa of the fibula → posterior talus
Strongest lateral ankle ligament; resists posterior talar shift
Rarely torn — needs a severe injury.
lig-posterior-tibiofibular-ligament: Back of the distal tibia → lateral malleolus
lig-pubic-symphysis: Fibrocartilaginous joint between the two pubic bones
lig-quadrate-ligament: Radial neck → radial notch of the ulna
lig-radioscaphocapitate-ligament: Main palmar stabiliser of the wrist
lig-sacrospinous-ligament: Separates the greater from the lesser sciatic foramen
Piriformis exits through the greater sciatic foramen; landmark for the pudendal nerve block (ischial spine).
lig-sacrotuberous-ligament: Sacrum/coccyx and posterior ilium → ischial tuberosity
Resists sacral tilting (nutation); forms the border of the sciatic foramina
With the sacrospinous ligament it converts the sciatic notches into the greater and lesser sciatic foramina.
lig-sphenomandibular-ligament: Spine of sphenoid → lingula of mandible
Landmark for the inferior alveolar nerve block.
lig-plantar-calcaneonavicular-ligament: "Spring ligament": supports the head of the talus and the medial longitudinal arch
lig-posterior-tibiotalar-ligament: Deepest, strongest part of the deltoid ligament
lig-radiate-ligament-of-head-of-rib: Rib head → two vertebral bodies and the disc
Fan-shaped support of the rib head
lig-scapholunate-interosseous-ligament: Tear → scapholunate dissociation ("Terry Thomas" gap on X-ray).
lig-superficial-part-of-tibial-collatera: Medial femoral epicondyle → medial surface of the tibia (deep to the pes anserinus)
The MCL (tibial collateral ligament) is fused to the medial meniscus — "Unhappy triad": ACL + MCL + medial meniscus from a blow to the lateral knee.
lig-superficial-transverse-metacarpal-li: Transverse fibres in the palm at the finger bases
lig-superior-extensor-retinaculum-of-ank: Tibia → fibula just above the ankle
lig-superior-fibular-retinaculum: Holds fibularis longus and brevis tendons behind the malleolus
lig-superior-transverse-scapular-ligamen: Converts the notch into a foramen
"Army over the bridge, Navy under": suprascapular artery passes over, nerve under.
lig-supraspinous-ligament: Tips of the spinous processes C7 → sacrum
Continues above C7 as the nuchal ligament.
lig-tibiocalcaneal-ligament: Medial malleolus → sustentaculum tali of the calcaneus
Part of the deltoid ligament; resists eversion
The deltoid ligament is so strong that eversion injuries often fracture the medial malleolus instead of tearing it.
lig-tibionavicular-ligament: Part of the deltoid ligament; resists eversion
Deltoid ligament = tibionavicular + tibiocalcaneal + anterior & posterior tibiotalar parts.
lig-transverse-humeral-ligament: Holds the long head of biceps tendon in its groove
lig-transverse-ligament-of-knee: Joins the anterior horns of the medial and lateral menisci
lig-transverse-part-of-iliofemoral-ligam: AIIS → intertrochanteric line (upper limb of the "Y")
Strongest ligament in the body (Y-ligament of Bigelow); prevents hyperextension
Lets you stand with almost no muscle effort — you "hang" on it.
lig-trapezoid-ligament: Coracoid process → trapezoid line of the clavicle
Suspends the scapula from the clavicle
lig-ulnar-collateral-ligament: Medial epicondyle → coronoid process and olecranon
"Tommy John" injury in throwers — reconstructed with a palmaris longus graft.
lig-patellar-ligament: Apex of the patella → tibial tuberosity
Continuation of the quadriceps tendon; transmits knee extension
Tapped for the knee-jerk (patellar) reflex, L3–L4 — femoral nerve. Osgood–Schlatter = traction at its tibial insertion.
lig-apical-ligament-of-dens: Tip of the dens → anterior margin of the foramen magnum (basion)
lig-transverse-ligament-of-atlas: Medial tubercles of the lateral masses of C1, passing behind the dens
Holds the dens against the anterior arch of the atlas so it cannot slip back into the spinal cord
Horizontal bar of the cruciate (cruciform) ligament. Lax in Down syndrome and rheumatoid arthritis → atlanto-axial instability.
lig-alar-ligament: Sides of the dens → medial sides of the occipital condyles
Check ligaments: limit rotation and side-bending of the head
Strong, short cords — tightened by turning the head; can tear in whiplash.
lig-tectorial-membrane: Back of the C2 body → clivus (inside the foramen magnum)
Upward continuation of the posterior longitudinal ligament; covers the dens and its ligaments from behind
PLL → tectorial membrane at C2: remember it as the PLL's "roof" (tectum) over the dens.
lig-anterior-atlanto-occipital-membrane: Anterior arch of C1 → anterior margin of the foramen magnum
Continuation of the anterior longitudinal ligament region above C1.
lig-posterior-atlanto-occipital-membrane: Posterior arch of C1 → posterior margin of the foramen magnum
Limits flexion; the vertebral artery and suboccipital nerve pass beneath its lateral edge
Equivalent of the ligamentum flavum between C1 and the skull.
lig-anterior-tibiotalar-ligament: Anterior border of the medial malleolus → medial neck of the talus
Part of the deltoid ligament; resists eversion and anterior talar shift
Deltoid ligament = anterior tibiotalar + tibionavicular + tibiocalcaneal + posterior tibiotalar.
lig-posterior-meniscofemoral-ligament: Posterior horn of the lateral meniscus → medial femoral condyle, passing BEHIND the PCL
Pulls the lateral meniscus along with the femur; backs up the PCL
lig-anterior-meniscofemoral-ligament: Posterior horn of the lateral meniscus → medial femoral condyle, passing IN FRONT of the PCL
Stabilises the lateral meniscus; assists the PCL
Ligament of Humphry (present in about half of knees).
lig-pectineal-ligament: Along the pectineal line of the superior pubic ramus (from the lacunar ligament laterally)
Strong fibrous band reinforcing the pectineal line
Cooper's ligament — the anchor for many hernia repairs; posterior boundary of the femoral ring.
lig-lacunar-ligament: Medial end of the inguinal ligament → pectineal line of the pubis
Curved triangular extension of the inguinal ligament
Medial boundary of the femoral ring — femoral hernias pass lateral to it.
lig-intertransverse-ligaments: Between the transverse processes of neighbouring vertebrae (thoracic and lumbar)
Limit side-bending to the opposite side
Thin in the thoracic region, membranous in the lumbar region.
lig-lateral-costotransverse-ligament: Tip of the transverse process → non-articular part of the rib tubercle
Strengthens the costotransverse joint from behind
lig-superior-costotransverse-ligament: Crest of the rib neck → lower border of the transverse process above
Suspends each rib from the vertebra above
The posterior ramus of the spinal nerve passes medial to it.
lig-lumbocostal-ligament: Transverse process of L1 → lower border of the 12th rib
lig-medial-arcuate-ligament: Body of L1 → transverse process of L1, arching over psoas major
Origin of diaphragm fibres; psoas slides beneath it
Covers psoas — "medial arcuate over psoas, lateral arcuate over QL".
lig-lateral-arcuate-ligament: Transverse process of L1 → 12th rib, arching over quadratus lumborum
lig-lateral-atlanto-occipital-ligament: Transverse process of the atlas → jugular process of the occipital bone
Limits lateral tilting of the head
lig-radiate-sternochondral-ligaments: Front of each costal cartilage (1–7) → fans out onto the sternum
Fibres blend with the sternal membrane. Rib 1 cartilage–sternum is a primary cartilaginous joint (synchondrosis); 2–7 are synovial.
lig-interchondral-ligaments: Between the borders of costal cartilages 5–9/10
Bind the lower cartilages into the costal margin
lig-xiphichondral-ligament: 7th costal cartilage → front of the xiphoid process
Holds the xiphoid to the costal margin
lig-costocoracoid-ligament: Thickened upper edge of the clavipectoral fascia
The cephalic vein, thoraco-acromial artery and lateral pectoral nerve pierce the clavipectoral fascia here.
lig-suprapleural-membrane: Transverse process of C7 → inner border of the 1st rib
Covers the dome of the pleura (Sibson fascia) and stops the lung apex bulging into the neck
lig-medial-patellofemoral-ligament: Medial border of the patella → femur between the adductor tubercle and medial epicondyle
Main restraint against the patella dislocating laterally
Torn in nearly every lateral patellar dislocation; MPFL reconstruction is the standard repair.
lig-patellotibial-ligaments: Lower borders of the patella → medial and lateral tibial condyles
Secondary stabilisers of the patella beside the patellar ligament
lig-bicipital-aponeurosis: Biceps tendon → deep fascia over the medial forearm flexors (to the ulna)
Spreads part of the biceps pull onto the ulna; roof over the brachial artery and median nerve
"Grace of God" fascia: protects the brachial artery and median nerve during venepuncture of the median cubital vein above it.
lig-long-radiolunate-ligament: Palmar rim of the distal radius → lunate
Stops the carpus sliding toward the ulna
lig-short-radiolunate-ligament: Palmar-ulnar rim of the radius → lunate
Holds the lunate on the radius
lig-radioscapholunate-ligament: Carries vessels to the scapholunate ligament (ligament of Testut)
lig-palmar-metacarpophalangeal-ligaments: Palmar plates: metacarpal neck → base of each proximal phalanx
Prevent hyperextension of the knuckles; grooved for the flexor tendons
Joined side to side by the deep transverse metacarpal ligament.
lig-calcaneometatarsal-ligament: Lateral process of the calcaneal tuberosity → base of the 5th metatarsal
Lateral band of the plantar aponeurosis; supports the lateral arch
lig-reflected-inguinal-ligament: Pubic tubercle region → linea alba, curving up behind the superficial inguinal ring
Reinforces the back of the superficial inguinal ring
lig-palmar-carpal-ligament: Thickening of the antebrachial fascia across the front of the wrist, proximal to the flexor retinaculum
Holds the long flexor tendons down
The ulnar nerve and artery pass between it and the flexor retinaculum (Guyon canal).
lig-ligamentum-mucosum: Infrapatellar plica — a synovial fold, remnant of the embryonic septum
lig-medial-temporomandibular-ligament: Medial side of the capsule, temporal bone → medial pole of the mandibular condyle
Supports the medial side of the TMJ
lig-costocoracoid-membrane: Sheet between subclavius/clavicle, coracoid process and 1st rib, down to pectoralis minor
Upper part of the clavipectoral fascia
Pierced by the cephalic vein, thoraco-acromial vessels and lateral pectoral nerve.
lig-vasto-adductor-membrane: Vastus medialis → adductor longus and magnus (middle third of the thigh)
Roof of the adductor (subsartorial) canal under sartorius
Canal contents: femoral artery and vein, saphenous nerve and nerve to vastus medialis.
lig-intra-articular-sternochondral-ligam: 2nd costal cartilage → manubriosternal junction, inside the joint
Divides the 2nd sternocostal joint into two cavities
The 2nd costal cartilage marks the sternal angle (of Louis) — count ribs from here.
lig-median-arcuate-ligament: Fibrous arch joining the right and left crura in front of the aorta (about T12/L1)
Forms the front of the aortic hiatus
"I 8 10 Eggs AT 12": the aorta passes behind this arch at T12. A low arch can compress the coeliac trunk (median arcuate ligament syndrome).
lig-anterior-atlantoaxial-membrane: Lower border of the anterior arch of C1 → front of the C2 body
Continuation of the anterior longitudinal ligament region
lig-posterior-atlantoaxial-membrane: Posterior arch of C1 → laminae of C2
Equivalent of the ligamentum flavum at C1–C2
The C2 spinal nerve emerges through it.
lig-anterior-atlantodental-ligament: Anterior arch of C1 → front of the dens
Small ligament in front of the dens
lig-superior-longitudinal-band-of-crucif: Transverse ligament of atlas → anterior margin of the foramen magnum
Upper limb of the cruciform (cross-shaped) ligament
Cruciform ligament = transverse ligament + superior and inferior longitudinal bands.
lig-inferior-longitudinal-band-of-crucif: Transverse ligament of atlas → back of the C2 body
Lower limb of the cruciform ligament
lig-sternal-membrane: Fibrous sheet over the front of the manubrium and body of the sternum
Formed by the blending of the radiate sternochondral ligaments and pectoralis major tendons
lig-perineal-membrane: Triangular sheet between the ischiopubic rami, below the pubic symphysis
Supports the pelvic organs; attachment for the external genitalia
Separates the deep perineal pouch (above) from the superficial pouch (below).
lig-transverse-perineal-ligament: Thickened front edge of the perineal membrane, just below the pubic arch
Leaves a gap below the arcuate pubic ligament for the deep dorsal vein of the penis/clitoris
